name: 천문대 둥근 지붕(큰 방 천장 띠 전체, 30×8) (dome vault)
label: atlas_biome_interior/plus/dome vault

surfaces.part: dome vault shell with stone tile courses and copper ribs
pale arc edge line at the base of the dome
stepped brick wall band below the arc
central starry-sky window slit with gold sill

answer.evidence: This is a face-on view of a vault ceiling band. The width profile widens steadily from 44 px at row 0 to about 410 px at row 63. That is a dome outline seen straight on, not a horizontal surface that widens and narrows like an ellipse. The tile courses curve with the shell and the copper ribs run vertically as ribs. No band ends in a front-edge line with eave shadow below it. The light arc at rows 75-76 separates the dome from the brick steps below, but the brick steps are a vertical wall face. The window slit and the bricks are all drawn as vertical faces with no horizontal surface. For a flat wall-mounted piece this is an elevation, not a three-quarter view.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate has 10 visible tones per tile, about the same as the hedge (9) but well below the stall (17) and the roofed well (20). Its near-flat coverage is 23%, the highest on the board; the references run 0-13%. The dome stone panels are mostly one dark grey-blue with only faint per-brick variation, and some panels are flat. The copper ribs have about 3-4 steps and the stone about 4, short of Beodeul's 5-6. The grey brick base steps are better, with per-brick shading and mortar lines. 93% of dark edge pixels are neutral, so the thin dark outline along the dome rim and the rib edges reads as a neutral line rather than a tinted material tone. Some of that is natural for grey stone, so I call it mixed. Overall it is clean and readable but shallower and flatter than the references, and when in doubt it fails.

surfaces.part: dome shell with stone courses and copper ribs
light-grey curved edge line along the dome's lower rim
stepped brick wall band under the dome

answer.evidence: The dome is drawn as a flat elevation: a curved silhouette (width grows from 44 to 410 over rows 0-63) filled with face-on stone courses and curved copper ribs. There is no horizontal top plane, no ellipse and no eave band. The light-grey curve at rows 75-79 is a thin 1-2 row lower edge line, not a top surface. Below it, a stepped brick wall (rows 80-127) is also a vertical face. The whole piece reads as a flat front view, which suits a wall-mounted ceiling band, but it has no top surface.

styleAnswer.evidence: The dome has a stone tile ramp of about 4 greys (light, mid, dark, deep) with brick courses and a few per-stone highlights. The copper ribs have 3-4 browns with gold bands, and the window strip is dotted with stars. Visible tones per tile are 10, against 9 for the hedge and 17-20 for the stall and well, so density is below the richer references but not far off. Near-flat coverage is 23%, against 0-13% for the references. That is the highest of the set and shows in the plain grey stone areas and the window's dark blue field. 93% of the dark edge pixels are near-neutral, so the outer rim looks like a grey-black line, while the ribs have brown edges. The outline reads as mixed to near_black, in contrast with Beodeul's tinted outlines. Shading and density are shallower than the Beodeul standard (5-6 steps, tinted outlines, no flat areas), and the neutral dark rim gives it a sticker-like look. When in doubt, fail.

surfaces.part: dome shell with stone tile courses and copper ribs
central starry window slit with gold sill
stepped brick wall band below the dome rim

answer.evidence: The dome shell (rows 0-76) is a sloped, tiled roof-like plane. Its tile courses curve with the dome and widen from 44 px at row 0 to 410 px at row 63. It ends in a 2-row light grey edge line at rows 75-76, followed by a dark shadow line at row 79. Below that, the stepped brick wall (rows 80-127) is the vertical front face. The central window slit and the copper ribs are vertical details on the shell and are not separate top surfaces. The shell's curved tiles are a borderline case: they could instead read as a flat front elevation. I counted them as a roof plane (c) because they sit above a clear edge line with a front face below.

styleAnswer.evidence: The dome has tidy stone-block courses, copper ribs with gold bands and a starry window. Its shading is shallower than the references, though. The grey stone reads as about 3-4 close steps per block. The copper ribs have about 3 steps, and the brick steps below are close to flat. Visible tones per tile (10) sit inside the reference range (9-20) but well under the stall (17) and well (20). Near-flat coverage is 23%, above every reference (0-13%), and the individual stone blocks and the large dark dome surface are mostly single-tone. 93% of the dark edge pixels are near-neutral, against 0-1% for the hedge and cheese stall, so the dome rim and block seams look like a neutral dark line rather than a tinted material tone. The copper ribs do seem to have a brownish edge, so I call the outline mixed. There is little per-block grain or per-stone highlight of the kind Beodeul uses. The piece is clean and readable but flatter and more sticker-like than the references, so it fails.

surfaces.part: dome shell with brass ribs and stone tiles (sloped roof-like plane)
central star-sky window slit with gold sill
stepped brick wall below the dome edge

answer.evidence: The silhouette widens steadily from 44 px at row 0 to about 410 px at row 63. This is a large curved dome shell with staggered stone-tile courses and curved brass ribs, which I read as a sloped roof plane (evidence c). It ends in a light-grey 2-row edge line at rows 75-76 (L=171 against L=78 above), followed by a dark 1-row shadow at row 79. Below that line is a stepped brick wall face of about 48 rows (rows 80-127). This is a wall-mounted band, so the dome is drawn as a curved, mostly face-on vault. It could also be read as a front elevation of a dome. I judged it by the roof plane, edge line and shadow, and the brick face below.

styleAnswer.evidence: The dome has a clear stone-block pattern, copper ribs with gold studs, and a starry window slit, so the structure reads well. The main stone ramp has only about 4 steps (dark slate, mid, light, a pale rim), and the copper ribs have about 3. Visible tones per tile are 10, against 17-20 for the cheese stall and the well and 9 for the hedge. That is lower than the richest references. Near-flat coverage is 23%, against 0-13% for the references. The flat areas are the dome panels between the block joints, the dark window band and the brick steps at the bottom. The dark edge pixels are 93% near-neutral, versus 0-1% for the stall and hedge. The dome's outer rim and the joints therefore read as a neutral dark line rather than a darker tint of the neighbouring stone. Per-block highlights and speckle are weaker than the per-tile or per-stone detail on the references. The result is a clean but somewhat flatter, more sticker-like piece than the Beodeul standard.
